metadata.title: Sterling Shepard - Back to practice squad
metadata.description: Shepard reverted to the Jets' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
metadata.analysis: Shepard was on the field for 17 of the Jets' 32 offensive snaps as the team finished with a time possession of 17:15, and he failed to haul in his lone target from Geno Smith. It was the second time this season that the veteran wide receiver was promoted from the practice squad, and he's eligible for one more elevation before the Jets would be required to sign him to the active roster. Shepard could be brought up for Week 5 against the Browns on Oct. 11 if Adonai Mitchell (finger) is not cleared to play.

metadata.title: Sterling Shepard - Elevated ahead of Week 4
metadata.description: The Jets elevated Shepard from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.
metadata.analysis: Shepard is set to suit up on game day for the second straight week. Last Sunday in Detroit, the veteran wideout logged a healthy workload of 30 offensive snaps -- third-most among New York wideouts -- and caught his only target for three yards. Shepard could also garner a significant role this Sunday with Adonai Mitchell again ruled out due to a finger injury.

metadata.title: Sterling Shepard - Reverts to practice squad
metadata.description: Shepard reverted to the Jets' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
metadata.analysis: In his first action of the season, Shepard played 30 of 66 offensive snaps in Sunday's loss to the Lions, though he was targeted just one time. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) battling an injury, Shepard could again be elevated ahead of next Sunday's game against the Bears. He has no fantasy appeal.

metadata.title: Sterling Shepard - Elevated for Sunday
metadata.description: The Jets elevated Shepard from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Shepard is set to suit up as the No. 6 wide receiver for the Jets in Sunday's game against the Lions. The new practice squad face was elevated for a scenario where Adonai Mitchell (finger) is unable to play in Sunday's contest. If Mitchell receives the green light, Shepard may spend his first elevation with the team inactive.

metadata.title: Sterling Shepard - Gets PS deal with NYJ
metadata.description: The Jets signed Shepard to the practice squad Tuesday, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Shepard failed to make the Texans' 53-man roster at the end of training camp after signing with the team Aug. 21. He'll get a fresh opportunity with the Jets, and he's a candidate to be elevated to the active roster for Week 2 against the Jets if rookie first-rounder Omar Cooper (ankle) is unable to play. Shepard appeared in 13 regular-season games for the Buccaneers in 2025, finishing with a 39-371-1 receiving line on 53 targets while adding four carries for 19 yards.

metadata.analysis: Sheppard makes his return to the Giants. He spent time in training camp with the Texans before he was released. He returns to a depth role in the Giants wide receiver room.

metadata.title: Sterling Shepard Joining Jets' Practice Squad
metadata.description: The New York Jets are signing veteran wide receiver Sterling Shepard to their practice squad, according to Mike Garafolo. Shepard had a brief stint with Houston late in the preseason before being released at final cuts, and now he's heading back to New Jersey after spending the first eight seasons of his career with the Giants. The timing makes sense for a Jets team dealing with some receiver injuries. Omar Cooper Jr. is week-to-week with an ankle sprain, while Tim Patrick was placed on injured reserve over the weekend. Shepard caught 39 passes for 371 yards and one touchdown in 13 games with Tampa Bay last season, so there is still some experience here if New York needs it. For now, though, this is only a practice-squad move. Shepard would need to be elevated before he can help on game day, and there is no reason for fantasy managers to add him in standard leagues yet.

metadata.title: Sterling Shepard - Cut loose by Houston
metadata.description: Shepard was released by the Texans on Sunday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
metadata.analysis: Shepard signed with Houston on Aug. 21 after trying out with the team, but he will now hit the open market again ahead of the 2026 campaign. The 33-year-old had a productive season with the Buccaneers in 2025, securing 39 of 53 targets for 371 yards and a touchdown over 13 regular-season contests while operating in a depth role. The wideout will likely find another suitor, but he hasn't exceeded 400 receiving yards in a season since 2020, making him an unappealing fantasy option.

metadata.title: Sterling Shepard released by Texans
metadata.description: The Texans released WR Sterling Shepard.
metadata.analysis: Shepard signed with Houston earlier in August. He will seek a depth role with another team heading into the season.

metadata.title: Sterling Shepard - Signing with Houston
metadata.description: Shepard is signing with Houston after trying out with the team Friday, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: With Jayden Higgins lost for the season due to a torn ACL, Houston is adding veteran depth at wide receiver in the form of Shepard and Zay Jones. Shepard caught 39 passes for 371 yards and a touchdown across 13 games for the Buccaneers in 2025, but his path to a meaningful role will depend on where he slots into the Texans' receiving mix.

metadata.title: Sterling Shepard signing with Texans
metadata.description: Veteran WR Sterling Shepard is signing with the Houston Texans
metadata.analysis: Shepard signs with the Texans following Jayden Higgins' season-ending injury. Unfortunately, at age 33, he remains with little to no value in fantasy.
